newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves FDI proposals worth $219 million.
newsitem.headline: India approves FDI proposals worth $219 million.

text.p: India on Tuesday approved 54 foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals involving a total investment of 7.85 billion rupees ($219.2 million), the Industry Ministry said.

"The approved projects are in the field of infrastructure, agribusiness, electronics, engineering, petroleum, consultancy services, medical diagnostic appliances, hospital projects, durgs and pharmaceuticals and mining services," the ministry said in a statement.
The proposals included one involving a foreign investment of 498.6 million rupees ($14 million) by Coats Viyella India to make industrial textiles and threads.
One proposal involved an investment of 525 million rupees ($14.6 million) by U.S.-based Cabot Corp to make carbon black.
A proposal for 420 million rupees ($11.7 million) involved computer firm Intel Services Inc to market Intel products and develop software.
Industry Minister Murasoli Maran also approved a proposal by India's Indorama Cement Ltd to make slag cement with investment by expatriate Indians amounting to 999.9 million rupees ($27.9 million).
The minister also approved an investment of 1.75 billion rupees ($48.8 million) by Volclay International to manufacture bentonite products, the statement said.
